reviews.comment: Not the best but not the worst. 222 is just a very difficult course but ross is alright. it was his first time teaching the course also. not the best during lecture but he was alright during office hours. He also adjusted the grade scale shortly after the first exam and that saved me when i got to the final :)

He's a great person and nice guy to talk to but the man can't teach undergrads. I didn't go to a single lecture after week 2 and learned everything the day before each exam and still got a B. Exam FRQs were fair but MCQs destroyed my grade. All of the attendance quiz passwords are crackable, just use random keywords from the lecture slides.

He was not a great lecturer, however, the tests were very fair. I pretty much only used his resources (slides, practice exams, textbook/hw problems) and got A's on all except for one I goofed on. The course is obviously hard because of the abstract topics, but I thought he was a fair/knowledgeable prof and if you put in the work you would do well.

His exams had FRQ's which weren't too bad, but the MCQ's were purely conceptual so you had to know the ins and outs of Relativity and QM. On top of that he's a bad lecturer so you had to self teach the extremely difficult theory. All the exams were curved so the mean was a 70, and the cutoff for a C was a 60 which was the saving grace of the class.

Least engaging lectures in my 3 years at A&M. Truly impossible to pay attention to. The concepts in this class are very high level but doing problems is very easy which makes getting through this class with a B pretty easy. If you want to learn anything try to take someone else.

Better than winfried teizer and he's a nice dude, but that's all I can really say that's good about him. He doesn't really teach and his exams are really difficult. All you can really do is pray that there's a curve so you'll never have to take this class again.
my friend like him, but he got an A. I was not able to do the same. Make friends and self-study.

Lectures are barely comprehensible, full of  "um, uh, uh" and he admitted that he hadn't taught the second half of this class before during lecture. The only actually useful resource from the class is the list of practice problems he assigns from the textbook. Prepare to learn everything yourself. And attendance is mandatory btw.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Just finished the final. He's a smart man who stumbles over his words and not good at explaining physics topics to students. Lectures are required for attendance but nobody pays attention because it goes over our heads. Good luck self-studying quantum physics for the exam. The homework and attendance questions are unforgiving. Better than Teizer.

lectures are long and boring, no one pays attention. u gotta go to class though because every lecture there's a canvas attendance quiz that he gives the password for in class. he gives some review material for the test but most people get cooked

Basically the lectures go over everyone's head and the average for the first two exams are 70 & 60. He's better than Tiezer but the stuff Ross lecture about is probably better for physics students than for engineering students. Like oh boy, time to get completely confused by spherical quantum relativistic harmonics with the Schrodinger equation.
He's very chill and cool. 206 is just a sucky class. in office hours (which there are plenty of) he tries to help you solve it and make sure you understand it. he's really nice :3
Seems like a chill dude but he can't teach. Just go for iClickers.

Professor Ross's lectures consisted of him standing at the edge of the class and whispering into his mic with unexplained scribbles on the board. He taught an important but difficult elementary class by reading off the slides word for word without explaining himself how to approach the problem, he's timid and quiet. IT IS DOABLE tho, j self study
You just show up to class for the iClicker, that's it. As someone else has stated, he's very much a research professor.

I had Professor Ross for 206, and he was not a very good lecturer. You can tell that he is a research professor. I learned more from the textbook, and his lectures weren't much help. Avoid him if you want a good professor and to learn in class.

The lectures for 206 were not helpful and he is terrible at teaching the material. I stopped attending classes after Exam 1 and pulled an A from just grinding the textbook and past practice exams. Your grades are always recoverable because of the LO system but be prepared to work for them. Good luck, you will need it.

Actually for Phys 206. He is extremely confusing. I would not have done good if I had not taken Phys in high school. I didn't even pay attention in class because of how confusing he was. If you have taken Phys already I would still recommend a different prof because the class is much harder than any AP class I took, Including AP Phys C.
Dr Ross just doesn't know how to teach. That's it. Prepare for pain this semester.

He's a really nice guy. Okay yes, I dropped the course; I know how that sounds. But I went to every lecture and did every problem in the textbook. I made sure I knew how to do every problem in the course that was given. However, his teaching made the content extremely confusing. The class is difficult, and he did not make it better.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Nice guy, terrible prof. Ross is extremely timid and, although he really knows what he teaches, he has a terrible way of getting his point across. Lectures, in my opinion, were a complete waste of time. Stopped going a quarter into the semester and almost pulled an A strictly from reading the textbook. Ironic enough, clicker questions cost me the A

He is a decent enough prof but this class is a weedout. He is very nice and helpful though and although he won't volunteer to help, it'll be there if you need it.  In my opinion the lab and recitation were the worst parts of this class; there is nothing wrong with Dr. Ross or his lectures, although they aren't particularly stellar.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I would take Dr. Ross again in a heart beat. His lectures exude professionalism and his expertise in Physics is clear from the get-go. He wastes little time and does his best to ensure your understanding as well. For such a difficult subject, he simplifies it as best as he can, and seems to care that students wish to do well. Take him if you can.

Dr. Ross is a decent prof that's always willing to help when you need it. He is sort of soft-spoken and timid. Overall, he is a really nice guy, but his lectures can be unclear sometimes, although he will do his best to help you out if you need some extra info.
